Thus each moment or derivative coordinate is the retained Taylor interval plus \([-E,E]\); graph and remote objective intervals, pooled products, covariance entries, and contrasts are obtained by the displayed rational interval operations on those enlarged coordinate intervals. At precision \(b\), each exact rational \(+,-,	imes,\div\) endpoint is immediately replaced by \(\lfloor2^bxfloor2^{-b}\) on a lower endpoint and \(\lceil2^bxceil2^{-b}\) on an upper endpoint; division by an interval containing zero fails that box. Precisions are tried as \(b_t=\min\{b_0+t\Delta b,b_{\mathrm{cap}}\}\) for \(0\leq t\leq\lceil(b_{\mathrm{cap}}-b_0)/\Delta bceil\), in increasing \(t\). Tasks are processed breadth first in this order: unordered wrong-graph pairs under \(\preceq_{\mathfrak G}\), same-graph remote pairs, single-graph chart cells, covariance, and precision. A nonterminal box is bisected at its rational midpoint in the coordinate maximizing width divided by original-box width, with the smallest parameter coordinate breaking ties; children are processed lower half first. On a product box the same normalized-width rule is applied to the concatenated coordinates, with the first coordinate in graph-order and parameter-order breaking ties. Objective trees stop at depth \(b_{\max}\), and chart trees at depth \(c_{\max}\). A wrong-graph leaf passes exactly when its tail-enlarged interval for \(\lVert m_{ oldsymbol d,\mathcal T}-m_{ oldsymbol d',\mathcal T}Vert_W^2\) has positive lower endpoint. A same-graph product leaf is discarded if the interval upper bound for \(\lVert\vartheta-\vartheta'Vert_2^2-r_{\mathrm{id}}^2\) is negative, passes whenever the lower endpoint of its corresponding moment-distance enclosure is positive, and otherwise is subdivided. Thus a boundary-straddling box passes as soon as positivity holds on its entire product box; this implies positivity on the box's remote feasible subset and requires no nonnegative lower endpoint for the distance constraint. For chart construction, inflate each terminal cell \(H\) to \(C=\Theta_{ oldsymbol d}\cap(H+[-r_{\mathrm{id}},r_{\mathrm{id}}]^{d_{ oldsymbol d}})\); sorted rational endpoints must cover \(\Theta_{ oldsymbol d}\), and every pair of base cells whose coordinatewise distance can be below \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) must have its two cells contained in a common inflated chart. At the chart center, take the outward interval midpoint matrix of \(J\), choose the lexicographically first \(d_{ oldsymbol d}\)-row submatrix with nonzero exact rational determinant, and set \(P\) to its rational inverse times that row selector. Put \(S=(PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T})/2\). Fixed-order interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\), with no pivoting, must certify \(S\succ0\); among the mesh \(\{k2^{-b}:0\leq k\leq2^b\}\), fixed binary search on \([0,1]\) returns the largest \(u\) for which \(S-uI\) has a positive interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\), and this is the chart's rational \(\underline\mu\). Independently, search the same dyadic mesh for the largest rational \(u\) for which \(J^{\mathsf T}J-u^2I\) passes the identical test, and set \(\underline\kappa=u\). Covariance and sandwich denominators must exclude zero, their fixed-order \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) solves must succeed, and outward evaluation gives \(\overline v_	au\), \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\), and \(w_{\mathrm{cert}}\). If \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), set \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\); if the remote feasible set is empty, set \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\). A valid simplex allocation with some row entering \(A_{\mathcal T}\) assigned zero mass is \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). Return \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) exactly when rank is full, all required leaves pass, chart coverage passes, every \(\underline\mu,\underline\kappa\), and \(b_{\mathrm{in}}\) is positive, all covariance tests pass, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\). Return \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) for exact rank defect, simplex failure, invalid boxes, or a collision only as follows. On a graph-pair product box \(X\) with rational midpoint \(x\), if one exists, choose the lexicographically first square row projection \(F\) of the moment difference whose midpoint Jacobian is nonsingular, put \(C=\operatorname{mid}(J_F(X))^{-1}\), and form \(K(x,X)=x-CF(x)+(I-CJ_F(X))(X-x)\) by the same interval operations. A collision is refuted only when \(K(x,X)\subset\operatorname{int}(X)\), the two parameter factors are disjoint, and every moment coordinate omitted from \(F\) is certified to the singleton interval \([0,0]\) on \(K(x,X)\). At exhausted depth or precision, failed coverage, a nonpositive or zero-containing required interval, or an upper well bound above \(N_{\max}\), return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). The output bounds are minima or maxima of the stated rational terminal bounds, and \(\Pi_{\mathrm{cert}}\) records every recurrence table, box, projection, \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factor, rounding endpoint, and terminal test; hence no heuristic or unspecified choice affects \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)\).
